newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat steady in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: French wheat steady in slow trade.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Tuesday in slow trade as most buyers kept to the sidelines, dealers said.
Trade traditionally slows down ahead of the Easter holidays and there will be a break in European Union grain tenders this week for Easter, they said.
"It is very quiet and buyers are not really around," said one dealer.

Little fresh export news was there to move prices, and exporters largely ignored news that Algeria re-launched a previously delayed import tender for 75,0000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat for April/May.
Standard April wheat into Rouen was bid at 895 francs per tonne and offered at 900 francs, unchanged from Monday.
In intra-EU business, firm French wheat prices were deterring buyers from the north of the European Union, dealers said.
Fob Creil wheat was quoted at 820 francs per tonne for April-May delivery but there was no trade.
Fob Rhine wheat for April-June was offered at 862.50 francs per tonne against 870 francs at the end of last week.
MATIF fob barge wheat futures for May were quoted at 928 francs per tonne, down three francs from Monday. Total volume was 107 lots at 1438 GMT.
